claim: β-cell regeneration increased markedly in npas4l mutants owing to the ectopic differentiation of β-cells in the mesenchyme.
source: Surprisingly, β-cell regeneration increased markedly in npas4l mutants owing to the ectopic differentiation of β-cells in the mesenchyme, a phenotype not previously reported in any models.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Ectopic β-cell formation in the mesenchyme has not been previously reported in any models.
source: Surprisingly, β-cell regeneration increased markedly in npas4l mutants owing to the ectopic differentiation of β-cells in the mesenchyme, a phenotype not previously reported in any models.
evidence: The authors state this is a novel phenotype not previously reported.

claim: The ectopic β-cells expressed endocrine markers of pancreatic β-cells.
source: The ectopic β-cells expressed endocrine markers of pancreatic β-cells, and also responded to glucose with increased calcium influx.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 2 showing co-expression of multiple endocrine markers.

claim: The ectopic β-cells responded to glucose with increased calcium influx.
source: The ectopic β-cells expressed endocrine markers of pancreatic β-cells, and also responded to glucose with increased calcium influx.
evidence: This is demonstrated by live calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The vast majority of ectopic β-cells has a mesodermal origin.
source: Through lineage tracing, we determined that the vast majority of these ectopic β-cells has a mesodermal origin.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing experiments using drl, npas4l, and etsrp promoters shown in Figures 4, 5, and 6.

claim: Ectopic β-cells were found in npas4l mutants.
source: Notably, ectopic β-cells were found in npas4l mutants as well as following knockdown of the endothelial/myeloid determinant Etsrp.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Ectopic β-cells were found following knockdown of the endothelial/myeloid determinant Etsrp.
source: Notably, ectopic β-cells were found in npas4l mutants as well as following knockdown of the endothelial/myeloid determinant Etsrp.
evidence: This is demonstrated by morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Under the perturbation of endothelial/myeloid specification, mesodermal cells possess a remarkable plasticity enabling them to form β-cells.
source: Together, these data indicate that under the perturbation of endothelial/myeloid specification, mesodermal cells possess a remarkable plasticity enabling them to form β-cells, which are normally endodermal in origin.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined lineage tracing and loss-of-function experiments.

claim: β-cells are normally endodermal in origin.
source: Together, these data indicate that under the perturbation of endothelial/myeloid specification, mesodermal cells possess a remarkable plasticity enabling them to form β-cells, which are normally endodermal in origin.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about β-cell development.

claim: The homozygous mutation of npas4l significantly increased the number of ins:H2BGFP-positive cells during the β-cell regeneration period.
source: The homozygous mutation of npas4l significantly increased the number of ins:H2BGFP-positive cells during the β-cell regeneration period (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly shown in the quantification in Figure 1C.

claim: A distinctive ectopic β-cell population was observed in the mesenchymal region outside of the pancreas in the npas4l−/− group.
source: In addition, we observed a distinctive ectopic β-cell population in the mesenchymal region outside of the pancreas in the npas4l−/− group, an ectopic location that was very rarely observed in the sibling controls (including both wild-type and heterozygous siblings).
evidence: This is shown in confocal images in Figure 1.

claim: Ectopic β-cells were very rarely observed in the sibling controls (including both wild-type and heterozygous siblings).
source: In addition, we observed a distinctive ectopic β-cell population in the mesenchymal region outside of the pancreas in the npas4l−/− group, an ectopic location that was very rarely observed in the sibling controls (including both wild-type and heterozygous siblings).
evidence: This is shown in the quantification in Figure 1C.

claim: The ectopic population of β-cells contributed to the major increase in the number of ins:H2BGFP-positive cells during β-cell regeneration.
source: This ectopic population of β-cells contributed to the major increase in the number of ins:H2BGFP-positive cells during β-cell regeneration (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is evident from the quantification separating pancreatic and ectopic β-cells in Figure 1C.

claim: The npas4l mutation did not enhance the survival of β-cells during the ablation.
source: Moreover, the comparable and sparse numbers of ins:DsRed-positive cells in the controls and mutants indicate that the npas4l mutation did not enhance the survival of β-cells during the ablation (Figure 1A,B) because the extended maturation time of DsRed (Baird et al., 2000) restricted the detection of DsRed to any surviving β-cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparable numbers of DsRed-positive cells and the known maturation time of DsRed.

claim: The extended maturation time of DsRed restricted the detection of DsRed to any surviving β-cells.
source: Moreover, the comparable and sparse numbers of ins:DsRed-positive cells in the controls and mutants indicate that the npas4l mutation did not enhance the survival of β-cells during the ablation (Figure 1A,B) because the extended maturation time of DsRed (Baird et al., 2000) restricted the detection of DsRed to any surviving β-cells.
evidence: This is based on the known properties of DsRed cited from Baird et al., 2000.

claim: There was a drastic reduction in the pancreas size in npas4l mutants.
source: To visualise the location of the ectopic β-cells better, we labelled the pancreas with ptf1a:EGFP expression and observed not only a drastic reduction in the pancreas size (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) but also the regeneration of β-cells clearly outside of the ptf1a-expressing exocrine pancreas in npas4l mutants (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: β-cells regenerated clearly outside of the ptf1a-expressing exocrine pancreas in npas4l mutants.
source: To visualise the location of the ectopic β-cells better, we labelled the pancreas with ptf1a:EGFP expression and observed not only a drastic reduction in the pancreas size (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) but also the regeneration of β-cells clearly outside of the ptf1a-expressing exocrine pancreas in npas4l mutants (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The majority of the ectopic β-cells formed in npas4l mutants intermingled with hand2:EGFP-positive mesenchymal cells between the pronephros and the pancreas.
source: By labelling the mesenchyme with hand2:EGFP expression (Figure 1F–K), we further revealed that the majority of the ectopic β-cells formed in npas4l mutants intermingled with hand2:EGFP-positive mesenchymal cells between the pronephros and the pancreas (Figure 1J,K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1J,K.

claim: Ectopic β-cells were occasionally observed intermingled with hand2:EGFP-positive mesenchymal cells ventral to the pancreas.
source: In addition, we occasionally observed ectopic β-cells intermingled with hand2:EGFP-positive mesenchymal cells ventral to the pancreas (Figure 1I,K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1I,K.

claim: The ectopic β-cells did not express hand2:EGFP.
source: Although the ectopic β-cells were located among the mesenchymal cells, they did not express hand2:EGFP.
evidence: This is evident from the lack of co-localization in Figure 1J,K.

claim: The majority of the ectopic β-cells co-expressed insulin and Isl1, neurod1, pdx1, mnx1, pcsk1, and ascl1b during β-cell regeneration.
source: Next, we examined multiple pancreatic endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, neurod1, pdx1, mnx1, pcsk1, and ascl1b (the functional homologue to Neurog3 in mammals), to validate the β-cell identity of the ectopic insulin-producing cells. The majority of the ectopic β-cells co-expressed insulin as well as these markers during β-cell regeneration (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2 and quantified in Table 1.

claim: ascl1b is the functional homologue to Neurog3 in mammals.
source: Next, we examined multiple pancreatic endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, neurod1, pdx1, mnx1, pcsk1, and ascl1b (the functional homologue to Neurog3 in mammals), to validate the β-cell identity of the ectopic insulin-producing cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Most of the β-cells in the ectopic population are likely functional based on high co-expression of pcsk1.
source: The high co-expression of pcsk1 (Figure 2R,S, Table 1), which encodes an enzyme necessary for insulin biosynthesis, indicates that most of the β-cells in the ectopic population are likely functional.
evidence: This is inferred from the high co-expression of pcsk1 shown in Figure 2R,S and Table 1.

claim: pcsk1 encodes an enzyme necessary for insulin biosynthesis.
source: The high co-expression of pcsk1 (Figure 2R,S, Table 1), which encodes an enzyme necessary for insulin biosynthesis, indicates that most of the β-cells in the ectopic population are likely functional.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about pcsk1 function.

claim: Not all ectopic β-cells expressed ascl1b:EGFP.
source: Consistent with previous findings in pancreatic β-cells, not all ectopic β-cells expressed ascl1b:EGFP (Figure 2V,W, Table 1), which suggests that ascl1b works as a transient endocrine cell fate regulator (Flasse et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2V,W and Table 1.

claim: ascl1b works as a transient endocrine cell fate regulator.
source: Consistent with previous findings in pancreatic β-cells, not all ectopic β-cells expressed ascl1b:EGFP (Figure 2V,W, Table 1), which suggests that ascl1b works as a transient endocrine cell fate regulator (Flasse et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Flasse et al., 2013.

claim: Lower co-expression levels of neurod1 and pdx1 were observed in ectopic β-cells compared with the pancreatic population in npas4l mutants.
source: In contrast with Isl1, mnx1, pcsk1, and ascl1b, we observed lower co-expression levels of neurod1 and pdx1 in ectopic β-cells compared with the pancreatic population in npas4l mutants (Table 1).
evidence: This is shown in Table 1 and Figure 2.

claim: The pdx1-expressing pancreatic duct was reduced in the npas4l mutant.
source: In addition to the reduction in pancreas size (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), the pdx1-expressing pancreatic duct was also reduced in the npas4l mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that the pancreas and its duct did not expand to form the ectopic β-cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pancreas and its duct did not expand to form the ectopic β-cells.
source: In addition to the reduction in pancreas size (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), the pdx1-expressing pancreatic duct was also reduced in the npas4l mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that the pancreas and its duct did not expand to form the ectopic β-cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduction in pancreas size and pdx1-expressing duct.

claim: The pancreatic and ectopic β-cells are similar, yet they are two distinct β-cell populations.
source: These observations together suggest that the pancreatic and ectopic β-cells are similar, yet they are two distinct β-cell populations.
evidence: This is inferred from the differences in marker expression and location.

claim: 66% of pancreatic β-cells displayed mild and basal levels of calcium activity at the baseline.
source: After β-cell ablation by MTZ and one day of β-cell regeneration, we found comparable proportions of pancreatic (66%) and ectopic (67%) β-cells displaying mild and basal levels of calcium activity at the baseline (Figure 3 and Video 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F.

claim: 67% of ectopic β-cells displayed mild and basal levels of calcium activity at the baseline.
source: After β-cell ablation by MTZ and one day of β-cell regeneration, we found comparable proportions of pancreatic (66%) and ectopic (67%) β-cells displaying mild and basal levels of calcium activity at the baseline (Figure 3 and Video 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F.

claim: 50% of pancreatic β-cells elicited calcium oscillations upon glucose treatment.
source: Upon glucose treatment, 50% of pancreatic β-cells and 33% of ectopic β-cells elicited calcium oscillations, suggesting that a portion of the pancreatic and ectopic β-cells have the ability to respond to glucose to secrete insulin in the npas4l mutants during β-cell regeneration.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F.

claim: 33% of ectopic β-cells elicited calcium oscillations upon glucose treatment.
source: Upon glucose treatment, 50% of pancreatic β-cells and 33% of ectopic β-cells elicited calcium oscillations, suggesting that a portion of the pancreatic and ectopic β-cells have the ability to respond to glucose to secrete insulin in the npas4l mutants during β-cell regeneration.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F.

claim: A portion of the pancreatic and ectopic β-cells have the ability to respond to glucose to secrete insulin in the npas4l mutants during β-cell regeneration.
source: Upon glucose treatment, 50% of pancreatic β-cells and 33% of ectopic β-cells elicited calcium oscillations, suggesting that a portion of the pancreatic and ectopic β-cells have the ability to respond to glucose to secrete insulin in the npas4l mutants during β-cell regeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the calcium oscillation data in response to glucose.

claim: npas4l expression is first initiated in the lateral plate mesoderm at the tailbud stage.
source: We have previously shown that npas4l expression is first initiated in the lateral plate mesoderm at the tailbud stage by in situ hybridisation (Reischauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work by Reischauer et al., 2016.

claim: npas4l was severely reduced in the lateral plate mesoderm in the npas4l mutants at 20 hpf.
source: In this study, we examined npas4l expression at 20 hr postfertilisation (hpf) and found that npas4l was severely reduced in the lateral plate mesoderm in the npas4l mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), whereas normal expression levels were observed in the tailbud and brain.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Normal npas4l expression levels were observed in the tailbud and brain in npas4l mutants.
source: In this study, we examined npas4l expression at 20 hr postfertilisation (hpf) and found that npas4l was severely reduced in the lateral plate mesoderm in the npas4l mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), whereas normal expression levels were observed in the tailbud and brain.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The cells with reduced npas4l expression were still present in the lateral plate mesoderm.
source: The cells with reduced npas4l expression were still present in the lateral plate mesoderm as demonstrated by the embryos incubated overnight to further develop the npas4l expression signal (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B'.

claim: There were no significant differences in the expression of the examined early mesodermal or endodermal transcription factors foxa2, gsc, and mixl1, or the pancreatic endocrine progenitor marker ascl1b in npas4l mutants.
source: On the contrary, there were no significant differences in the expression of the examined early mesodermal or endodermal transcription factors foxa2, gsc, and mixl1, or the pancreatic endocrine progenitor marker ascl1b (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–J.

claim: npas4l can act cell-autonomously to affect the hematopoietic and endothelial lineages.
source: Because the ectopic β-cells induced by the npas4l mutation also resided in the mesenchymal region, and npas4l can act cell-autonomously to affect the hematopoietic and endothelial lineages (Parker and Stainier, 1999), we hypothesised that the ectopic β-cells originated from a mesodermal lineage.
evidence: This is cited from Parker and Stainier, 1999.

claim: The spatial expression pattern of drl in the npas4l mutants resembled that in the sibling controls.
source: The spatial expression pattern of drl in the npas4l mutants resembled that in the sibling controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting that npas4l mutation did not induce any ectopic expression of drl to disrupt the lineage-tracing approach.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: npas4l mutation did not induce any ectopic expression of drl to disrupt the lineage-tracing approach.
source: The spatial expression pattern of drl in the npas4l mutants resembled that in the sibling controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting that npas4l mutation did not induce any ectopic expression of drl to disrupt the lineage-tracing approach.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar expression patterns.

claim: 98.9% of the ectopic β-cells in the mesenchymal region were mCherry-positive, indicating they derived from the drl-expressing mesodermal cells.
source: Furthermore, 98.9% of the ectopic β-cells in the mesenchymal region were mCherry-positive (Figure 4H'–H'''), indicating that they derived from the drl-expressing mesodermal cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4H'–H''' and quantified in Figure 4D.

claim: Knocking down etsrp led to the formation of ectopic β-cells.
source: Similar to the npas4l mutation, knocking down etsrp led to the formation of ectopic β-cells (Figure 4I–L''').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4I–L'''.

claim: Co-injecting lower doses of two different etsrp morpholinos (MO1 and MO2) exerted a synergistic effect on ectopic β-cell emergence.
source: Co-injecting lower doses of two different etsrp morpholinos (MO1 and MO2) exerted a synergistic effect on ectopic β-cell emergence (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), suggesting that the phenotype was not due to an off-target effect.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The ectopic β-cell phenotype was not due to an off-target effect of etsrp morpholinos.
source: Co-injecting lower doses of two different etsrp morpholinos (MO1 and MO2) exerted a synergistic effect on ectopic β-cell emergence (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), suggesting that the phenotype was not due to an off-target effect.
evidence: This is inferred from the synergistic effect of two different morpholinos.

claim: 94.3% of the ectopic β-cells in etsrp morphants was lineage-traced back to the drl-expressing mesodermal cells.
source: The majority of the ectopic β-cells (94.3%) in etsrp morphants was also lineage-traced back to the drl-expressing mesodermal cells, suggesting that the ectopic β-cell formation was also of mesodermal origin following etsrp knockdown.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4J and L'–L'''.

claim: The ectopic β-cell formation was of mesodermal origin following etsrp knockdown.
source: The majority of the ectopic β-cells (94.3%) in etsrp morphants was also lineage-traced back to the drl-expressing mesodermal cells, suggesting that the ectopic β-cell formation was also of mesodermal origin following etsrp knockdown.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage tracing data.

claim: 32.6% of ectopic β-cells could be traced back to the npas4l lineage.
source: Some of these ectopic β-cells (32.6%) could be traced back to the npas4l lineage as they were labelled by ubb:mCherry after the Cre-recombination driven by npas4l:Gal4 and UAS:Cre (Figure 5C and E–E'''), which further supports a mesodermal origin of the ectopic β-cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C and E–E'''.

claim: The ectopic β-cells emerged in close proximity to mesodermal cells with active npas4l expression in the transheterozygous npas4ls5/bns423 mutants.
source: The ectopic β-cells emerged in close proximity to mesodermal cells with active npas4l expression in the transheterozygous npas4ls5/bns423 mutants (Figure 5G–G''').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G–G'''.

claim: No ectopic β-cells with EGFP expression were observed, suggesting that these mesodermal cells have lost the identity of the lateral plate mesoderm with npas4l expression.
source: However, we did not observe any ectopic β-cells with EGFP expression, suggesting that these mesodermal cells have lost the identity of the lateral plate mesoderm with npas4l expression and started to express insulin as in the endodermal pancreatic β-cells instead.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of EGFP expression in ectopic β-cells shown in Figure 5G–G'''.

claim: The mesodermal cells started to express insulin as in the endodermal pancreatic β-cells.
source: However, we did not observe any ectopic β-cells with EGFP expression, suggesting that these mesodermal cells have lost the identity of the lateral plate mesoderm with npas4l expression and started to express insulin as in the endodermal pancreatic β-cells instead.
evidence: This is inferred from the insulin expression in cells without npas4l expression.

claim: The majority of kdrl-expressing endothelial cells were being traced in the intersegmental vessels (86.6%).
source: We validated the efficiency of the etsrp-lineage tracer and revealed that the majority of kdrl-expressing endothelial cells were being traced in the intersegmental vessels (86.6%) and other vasculature (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: 73.9% of the ectopic β-cells were labelled in red, illustrating that the etsrp-expressing lineage gave rise to a significant portion of the ectopic β-cells.
source: After β-cell ablation by MTZ treatment at 1–2 dpf and β-cell regeneration for 30 hr ectopic β-cells formed in the etsrp morphants, and 73.9% of the ectopic β-cells were labelled in red (Figure 6B–E'''), illustrating that the etsrp-expressing lineage gave rise to a significant portion of the ectopic β-cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B–E'''.

claim: The co-localisation of insulin staining and the nuclear green tracer confirms the mesodermal lineage of the ectopic β-cells.
source: The co-localisation of insulin staining and the nuclear green tracer further confirms the mesodermal lineage of the ectopic β-cells (Figure 6G–G''').
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6G–G'''.

claim: The ectopic β-cell formation is not restricted to the loss of a specific gene, but rather due to the perturbation of endothelial/myeloid specification.
source: Together, we used three different lineage-tracing models as well as three different loss of function models, that is using the promoter of drl, npas4l, or etsrp to drive Cre in npas4ls5/s5 mutants, npas4ls5/bns423 mutants, or etsrp morphants. This suggests that the ectopic β-cell formation is not restricted to the loss of a specific gene, but rather due to the perturbation of endothelial/myeloid specification.
evidence: This is inferred from the multiple different models all showing the same phenotype.

claim: The ectopic β-cells were likely functional because they expressed several endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, mnx1, and pcsk1.
source: We then unexpectedly revealed β-cells regenerating ectopically in the mesenchymal area. The ectopic β-cells were likely functional because they expressed several endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, mnx1, and pcsk1, and were capable of responding to glucose to induce calcium oscillations during β-cell regeneration, although we do not know if they possess all the features of bona fide β-cells.
evidence: This is inferred from marker expression and functional assays.

claim: The ectopic β-cells were capable of responding to glucose to induce calcium oscillations during β-cell regeneration.
source: We then unexpectedly revealed β-cells regenerating ectopically in the mesenchymal area. The ectopic β-cells were likely functional because they expressed several endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, mnx1, and pcsk1, and were capable of responding to glucose to induce calcium oscillations during β-cell regeneration, although we do not know if they possess all the features of bona fide β-cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3.

claim: It is not known if the ectopic β-cells possess all the features of bona fide β-cells.
source: We then unexpectedly revealed β-cells regenerating ectopically in the mesenchymal area. The ectopic β-cells were likely functional because they expressed several endocrine and β-cell markers, including Isl1, mnx1, and pcsk1, and were capable of responding to glucose to induce calcium oscillations during β-cell regeneration, although we do not know if they possess all the features of bona fide β-cells.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this limitation.

claim: The data demonstrated the plasticity of β-cell differentiation across the committed germ layers in vivo.
source: Our data demonstrated the plasticity of β-cell differentiation across the committed germ layers in vivo, i.e., switching from a mesodermal to an endodermal fate in a regenerative setting, while gastrulation and cell fate commitment in the germ layers are considered to be irreversible in development.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage tracing data showing mesodermal origin of β-cells.

claim: Gastrulation and cell fate commitment in the germ layers are considered to be irreversible in development.
source: Our data demonstrated the plasticity of β-cell differentiation across the committed germ layers in vivo, i.e., switching from a mesodermal to an endodermal fate in a regenerative setting, while gastrulation and cell fate commitment in the germ layers are considered to be irreversible in development.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Ectopic pancreata have been observed in Hes1 mutant mice.
source: Ectopic pancreata have been observed before, e.g., in Hes1 mutant mice (Fukuda, 2006; Sumazaki et al., 2004), although that has been shown to be through an expansion of the pancreas rather than through changes in cell fate determination across organs or germ layers (Jørgensen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Fukuda, 2006 and Sumazaki et al., 2004.

claim: Ectopic pancreata in Hes1 mutant mice have been shown to be through an expansion of the pancreas rather than through changes in cell fate determination across organs or germ layers.
source: Ectopic pancreata have been observed before, e.g., in Hes1 mutant mice (Fukuda, 2006; Sumazaki et al., 2004), although that has been shown to be through an expansion of the pancreas rather than through changes in cell fate determination across organs or germ layers (Jørgensen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Jørgensen et al., 2018.

claim: This discovery is the first demonstration of ectopic β-cells with a mesodermal origin in vivo.
source: Our discovery is, to our knowledge, the first demonstration of ectopic β-cells with a mesodermal origin in vivo.
evidence: The authors state this is novel to their knowledge.

claim: npas4l plays a crucial role in the early specification of endothelium and blood.
source: The recent genome-wide study with zebrafish embryos has confirmed the crucial role of npas4l in the early specification of endothelium and blood as the expressions of some endothelial and hematopoietic genes like tal1, etsrp, lmo2, gfi1aa, and gata1a were downregulated in homozygous npas4l mutants (Marass et al., 2019), suggesting that some populations of mesodermal cells may not have acquired their designated cell fates and remained in a more plastic state.
evidence: This is cited from Marass et al., 2019.

claim: The expressions of some endothelial and hematopoietic genes like tal1, etsrp, lmo2, gfi1aa, and gata1a were downregulated in homozygous npas4l mutants.
source: The recent genome-wide study with zebrafish embryos has confirmed the crucial role of npas4l in the early specification of endothelium and blood as the expressions of some endothelial and hematopoietic genes like tal1, etsrp, lmo2, gfi1aa, and gata1a were downregulated in homozygous npas4l mutants (Marass et al., 2019), suggesting that some populations of mesodermal cells may not have acquired their designated cell fates and remained in a more plastic state.
evidence: This is cited from Marass et al., 2019.

claim: Some populations of mesodermal cells may not have acquired their designated cell fates and remained in a more plastic state in npas4l mutants.
source: The recent genome-wide study with zebrafish embryos has confirmed the crucial role of npas4l in the early specification of endothelium and blood as the expressions of some endothelial and hematopoietic genes like tal1, etsrp, lmo2, gfi1aa, and gata1a were downregulated in homozygous npas4l mutants (Marass et al., 2019), suggesting that some populations of mesodermal cells may not have acquired their designated cell fates and remained in a more plastic state.
evidence: This is inferred from the downregulation of cell fate specification genes.

claim: There was a significant reduction in the cell clusters of endothelial cells and endothelial progenitor cells in homozygous etsrp mutants in a single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
source: In line with the important role of etsrp in the endothelial cell fate determination, Chestnut et al., 2020 have reported a significant reduction in the cell clusters of endothelial cells and endothelial progenitor cells in homozygous etsrp mutants in a single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
evidence: This is cited from Chestnut et al., 2020.

claim: There was a remarkable increase in the cluster of lateral plate mesoderm in homozygous etsrp mutants.
source: Interestingly, they have also shown a remarkable increase in the cluster of lateral plate mesoderm, which points to the possibility that a larger pool of more versatile mesodermal cells remained in the homozygous etsrp mutants.
evidence: This is cited from Chestnut et al., 2020.

claim: A larger pool of more versatile mesodermal cells may have remained in the homozygous etsrp mutants.
source: Interestingly, they have also shown a remarkable increase in the cluster of lateral plate mesoderm, which points to the possibility that a larger pool of more versatile mesodermal cells remained in the homozygous etsrp mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in lateral plate mesoderm cluster.

claim: The versatile lateral plate mesoderm close to the pancreas could contribute to the β-cell regeneration in npas4l mutants or etsrp morphants.
source: Since we could trace the origin of ectopic β-cells back to drl, npas4l, and etsrp lineages, we believe that the versatile lateral plate mesoderm close to the pancreas could contribute to the β-cell regeneration in npas4l mutants or etsrp morphants.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage tracing data.

claim: The mechanisms of ectopic β-cell formation in npas4l mutants and etsrp morphants could be different.
source: Before deciphering these mechanisms, we cannot formally rule out the possibility that the mechanisms of ectopic β-cell formation in npas4l mutants and etsrp morphants could be different.
evidence: The authors acknowledge this as a possibility.

claim: The mutated gene in the cloche mutant was named npas4l because its encoded protein shares homology with human NPAS4.
source: The mutated gene in the cloche mutant was named npas4l because its encoded protein shares homology with human NPAS4 (Reischauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from Reischauer et al., 2016.

claim: Injecting human NPAS4 mRNA or zebrafish npas4l mRNA into zebrafish cloche mutant embryos at the one-cell stage could rescue the mutants.
source: Although injecting human NPAS4 mRNA or zebrafish npas4l mRNA into zebrafish cloche mutant embryos at the one-cell stage could rescue the mutants, Npas4 knockout mice are unlikely to share the same severe vascular and hematopoietic defects as zebrafish npas4l mutants because Npas4 knockout mice survive to adulthood (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a known result.

claim: Npas4 knockout mice are unlikely to share the same severe vascular and hematopoietic defects as zebrafish npas4l mutants because Npas4 knockout mice survive to adulthood.
source: Although injecting human NPAS4 mRNA or zebrafish npas4l mRNA into zebrafish cloche mutant embryos at the one-cell stage could rescue the mutants, Npas4 knockout mice are unlikely to share the same severe vascular and hematopoietic defects as zebrafish npas4l mutants because Npas4 knockout mice survive to adulthood (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from the survival of Npas4 knockout mice cited from Lin et al., 2008.

claim: Other members of the mammalian NPAS protein family or other proteins may be functionally redundant with NPAS4 in vascular and hematopoietic development.
source: This discrepancy suggests that other members of the mammalian NPAS protein family or other proteins may be functionally redundant with NPAS4 in vascular and hematopoietic development.
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between zebrafish and mouse phenotypes.

claim: Mammalian NPAS4 has been shown to have important cell-autonomous functions in β-cells.
source: Mammalian NPAS4 has been shown to have important cell-autonomous functions in β-cells (Sabatini et al., 2018; Speckmann et al., 2016).

claim: In zebrafish, npas4a is the main npas4 paralogue expressed in β-cells.
